statement: George Long's English translation of Marcus Aurelius's Meditations was published in 1862, and Long died in 1879.
source: Marcus Aurelius, The Thoughts of the Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, trans. George Long (London, 1862); Project Gutenberg eBook #15877 front matter
notes: Basis of MEDITATIONS_EDITION_SOURCE_REPORT_TR.md; translation is public domain worldwide (life+70 expired 1949).

statement: The Meditations comprise twelve books with 487 numbered sections in the canonical division: 17, 17, 16, 51, 36, 59, 75, 61, 42, 38, 39, 36.
source: Project Gutenberg eBook #15877, section structure verified during typesetting
notes: Used as the canonical-structure check in the ebook pipeline CLEANUP step.

statement: Henry Ernest Dudeney's The Canterbury Puzzles was published in 1907 and Amusements in Mathematics in 1917; Dudeney died in 1930.
source: Project Gutenberg eBooks #27635 and #16713 (title pages); Dudeney's dates per the Gutenberg author record
notes: Both volumes pre-1931 → US public domain; life+70 expired 2001.

statement: Lafcadio Hearn's Kwaidan: Stories and Studies of Strange Things was published by Houghton Mifflin in 1904, the year of Hearn's death.
source: Project Gutenberg eBook #1210 title page; Internet Archive kwaidanstoriesst00hearuoft
notes: Text is public domain worldwide. The first edition's plates by Keishū Takénouchi are a separate rights question (see rights ledger).

statement: Edward Falkener's Games Ancient and Oriental and How to Play Them was published by Longmans, Green in 1892; Falkener lived 1814–1896.
source: Internet Archive item gamesancientorie00falkuoft (possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT); title page
notes: Not on Project Gutenberg; any claimed PG number is false.

statement: Codex Bestiarium contains 112 creature entries, not 120.
source: Build reports in the CODEX_BESTIARIUM repository (entries: 112; plate-consistency measured 112, accepted 112) and the PDF's own metadata
notes: All four live Amazon listings still say 120 — a metadata error to correct in KDP.

statement: KDP pays 60% of list price on paperbacks priced at or above $9.99 on Amazon.com (50% below), 40% through Expanded Distribution, less printing cost; hardcover printing on Amazon.com is $5.65 plus $0.012 per page for black ink.
source: KDP Help: Paperback Royalty (G201834330) and the KDP printing cost tables
notes: Rate card also encoded in scripts/strategy/price-engine.mjs.

statement: Books consisting primarily of public-domain content are only eligible for the 35% Kindle royalty option, and a differentiated public-domain edition must be translated, annotated or carry ten or more original illustrations, with the corresponding tag in the title field.
source: KDP Help: Publishing Public Domain Content (G200743940); KDP Digital Book Pricing
notes: Linked TOC, formatting improvements, collections and freely available internet content do not count as differentiation.
